summary:
Round-four machine validation passed with zero errors. Historical validation passed in rounds one through three. I independently matched outputs/demo-02/logistics-r4/logistics.json to the Markdown agenda and occupied staffing cells. Six continuous local-time blocks run in brief order: welcome and check-in 16:00–16:25, icebreaker 16:25–16:45, career panel 16:45–17:30, structured networking 17:30–18:15, refreshment break 18:15–18:40, and closing activity 18:40–19:00. The plan uses six volunteers. V4 checks the full step-free route, restroom and seating layout, handles accommodation requests, maintains access coverage during desk handoffs and provides seated refreshments. Accessible materials, spoken and written updates, seated or written participation and quiet seating are supported. V6 has a printed-material and spoken-cue fallback for AV or Wi-Fi failure. V3 checks speakers at 16:35, reallocates questions or runs facilitated peer discussion. V1 or acting V3 coordinates absences and shortage purchasing.

Recomputed catalog costs and compared both Markdown supply tables with outputs/demo-02/budget-r3/budget.json. SNACK10 is 3 packs of 10 at 1400 cents for 4200, FRUIT10 is 3 of 10 at 1000 for 3000, WATER24 is 3 of 24 at 800 for 2400, TAG25 is 3 of 25 at 450 for 1350, MARKER4 is 2 of 4 at 350 for 700, and PRINT25 is 3 of 25 at 650 for 1950. Coverage is 60 food servings, 72 drinks and 75 tags for 50 students, plus eight shared markers and 75 printed copies. Both plans allocate 50 double-sided large-print agendas with prompts and 25 copies for signs or backups. Budget calls for confirming the double-sided and mixed-batch print assumptions before ordering. The venue, tables, chairs, projector and Wi-Fi are free. The 13600-cent subtotal and 16400-cent reserve sum to the 30000-cent cap. Up to 13400 cents can fund shortages while retaining the 3000-cent reserve floor. The optional one-pack snack-to-fruit substitution keeps 60 servings and saves 400 cents, subject to dietary, labeling and supply updates.

Checked each Marketing r4 piece on its own. Instagram, flyer and email each give Women in Tech: Connect & Grow, Friday, February 19, 2027, 16:00–19:00 local time, room for 50 college students, all six activities in the same time slots, and [Venue], [RSVP link] and [Accessibility contact]. The flyer and email use [Speaker names]. Instagram names no speakers. The email's seated icebreaker, panel format, three 10-minute networking rounds and closing recap match Logistics. The participation and agenda-format promises are supported and the flyer and email's one-food and one-drink offer is covered by Budget. Logistics' Marketing revision 2 note refers to schedule and participation content that carried forward to r4.

Rechecked logistics-v5-refreshment-handoff. Round one identified a substantive gap in Logistics r1's volunteer-absence row, which moved V2 to the station only during the break, and Budget r1's shortage bullet, which relied on V5 and V1. The round-two verification cited Logistics r2's If V5 is absent and Budget r2 steps 1–4. Logistics r4's same section and Budget r3 steps 1–4 retain V2's pre-opening count, separate staging and item-level escalation, with a stock recheck and reassignment of prompts or questions if V5 leaves before service. V2 checks food and drink labels before V6 releases attendees. During service V6 pauses the queue while V2 consolidates, reconciles distributed servings, stages usable stock and rechecks both labels. V2 clears V6 to restart and tracks first servings while V4 continues seated delivery. Both files hold seconds during shortages, prioritize outstanding first servings and require checks on replacement labels. The accepted improvement still holds.

Rechecked logistics-v1-program-handoff. Logistics r1's absence row transferred coordination and cues but left public-facing duties unassigned. The If V1 is absent table accepted in Logistics r2 still works in Logistics r4. V3 takes the current block immediately, covers imminent cues, decides admission after V4's route check, receives speakers, gives the 16:22 welcome and 16:25 start cue, leads the icebreaker and calls its 16:42 wrap-up. V2 or accepting V6 covers check-in, agendas and tags. V3 announces and times the panel while moderating, with V6 on AV and networking instructions when available and the desk-specific fallback when needed. V6 calls networking rounds and staggers release. V3 announces the serving rule, authorizes replenishment under Budget r3 step 3 and gives the 18:35 return cue, then leads reflection and sharing, reads the recap and dismisses by 19:00. No material regression found.

Rechecked logistics-dual-absence-welcome-coverage. The Logistics r3 opening desk table and Budget r3 step 1 accepted in round three still agree with the Logistics r4 opening desk table. For both absences before doors open, V6 confirms readiness to V3 and covers first arrivals unless V2 confirms readiness to open. If V5 leaves while V1 is already absent, V2 stays until V6 accepts in person, on either side of 16:22. If V5 is absent first, V6 is stationed beside the desk during stock work and takes over immediately if V1 departs, continues if already covering, or accepts in person from V2 if V2 owns the desk. If V1 remains present, V1 hands over at 16:22 to V2 if back or V6 if stock work continues. V2 reports any deficit before returning, receives a briefing and explicitly accepts before V6 leaves, or resumes tag support until 16:22 if V1 still owns the desk. V4 remains on access and V3 gives the welcome as acting lead. If V6 still owns the desk at 16:38 with V1 absent, V6 alerts V2 and V3 and stays with arrivals. V2 pauses stock work, briefs and stages speakers by 16:42 while V3 wraps the icebreaker, then completes stock work and accepts the desk. V3 starts the 16:45 panel in discussion format if V6 remains at check-in. No material regression found. All three carried findings are verified and the independent audit found no further material issue.

verified.evidence: The Budget handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md pointed to Budget revision 1, whose shortage bullet named only V5 and V1. The handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md linked to ../budget-r2/budget.md#refreshment-shortage-procedure, whose step 1 lacked the mid-welcome transfer and speaker fallback. The handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r4/logistics.md now links to ../budget-r3/budget.md#refreshment-shortage-procedure. Resolved from that file's directory, this opens the Refreshment shortage procedure heading in outputs/demo-02/budget-r3/budget.md. Step 1 agrees with Logistics r4 on V6's desk coverage and in-person acceptance, V2's return acceptance and the 16:38, 16:42 and 16:45 fallbacks. Steps 2–4 agree on usable surplus and recount, first-serving priority including seated requests, holding seconds, immediate item-level reporting directly from V2 to acting V3 when V1 and V5 are absent, and V1 or acting V3 authorizing timely replenishment. Round the remaining deficits separately to whole FRUIT10 or WATER24 packs within the 13400-cent cumulative draw, retaining 3000 cents. Budget r3's reciprocal links resolve to Logistics r3's supply table and V5 opening desk handoff, which agree with the r4 sections on quantities and operational steps. Budget's Review note describes the former r3 link, which r4 has corrected.

In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md, Volunteer assignments and Setup and accessibility gave V2 the 16:22 desk handoff and written changes. The V2 absence row only consolidated questions and refreshments. In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r4/logistics.md, If V2 is absent assigns V1 the opening desk when present, including agendas, tags and markers, until V6 accepts in person by 16:22. If V2 leaves before that time, V1 retains the desk until V6 accepts. If V2 leaves after taking the desk, V1 takes over immediately, pausing the welcome as needed, until V6 explicitly accepts. If both V1 and V2 are absent from opening, V3 confirms V6's readiness before first arrivals. If their absences overlap during welcome, V3 sends V6 to take the post immediately or confirms existing V6 coverage, with an in-person transfer if V2 is still onsite. V4 stays on access. The spoken-cue owner gives V6 the change and cue time in advance or signals last-minute changes immediately. V6 posts large-print updates and hands them out on request at the desk, then maintains the entry posting and places a copy in the active area after moving to networking. V6 posts before speaking or directing movement when possible and updates at the next safe pause if a change arises during movement. With V6 on the desk through the panel, V3 stages speakers around the wrap-up if acting lead, runs discussion at 16:45 and takes questions directly. The lead gives networking instructions, then V6 posts desk directions before moving. Agenda prompts support the written table and closing, V5 runs the combined station and tracks first servings, and V4 continues seated delivery.

In outputs/demo-02/marketing-r3/marketing.md, the accessibility paragraph in each of Instagram caption, Flyer wording and Promotional email states that the route from arrival to seating, refreshments and the restroom is step-free. In outputs/demo-02/marketing-r4/marketing.md, each of those three paragraphs says the full step-free route is planned and pending verification before doors open, that verified route information will be shared through [RSVP link] and at check-in, and that attendees can contact [Accessibility contact]. This matches Setup and accessibility in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r4/logistics.md. V4 checks the route from arrival through entry to seating, refreshments and the accessible restroom, coordinates a verified alternative entrance or room if needed and directs arrivals there. V1 or acting V3 holds admission pending an accessible route.
